messages.subject: column selectors without hard-coding them
parts: How can I write a shiny app that creates (say) a drop-down of column selectors without hardcoding them in? For example, I would like it to read any csv file into a data frame and create the drop down without me having to know what is in the file before hand. Does this require a bit of meta-programming in R or can shiny handle this on its own?

messages.author: c6ca7877bef91eef
messages.subject: Re: column selectors without hard-coding them
parts:
You can get Dynamic UI in Shiny applications using renderUI and uiOutput. Here is a minimal example, that allows you to read csv files with header, using comma as separator, and creates a dropdown menu with column names. The idea is to push the code creating the selectInput to the server side, so that it can be dynamic and make use of the csv file that is being uploaded by the user. Hope this is useful!

runApp(list(
  ui = pageWithSidebar(
    headerPanel("CSV Viewer"),
    sidebarPanel(
      fileInput('file1', 'Choose CSV File',
        accept=c('text/csv', 'text/comma-separated-values,text/plain')),
      uiOutput('columns')
    ),
    mainPanel()
  ),
  server = function(input, output){
    output$columns <- renderUI({
      inFile <- input$file1
      if (is.null(inFile))
        return(NULL)
      
      dat = read.csv(inFile$datapath, header = T)
      selectInput("cols", "Column Names", names(dat))
    })
  }
  
))

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: column selectors without hard-coding them
parts:
Or use updateSelectInput (probably the preferred approach these days).

In your server function (since we need the "session" object, make sure your Shiny server function has the signature function(input, output, session) ):

observe({
  if (is.null(input$file1))
    return()
  dat <- read.csv(inFile$datapath, header = T)
  updateSelectInput(session, "cols", choices = names(dat))
})
